title: Choose covered call strikes from your view at expiration
summary: Covered call strike choice depends on your view of the stock at expiry. Bullish: strike out of the money. Expect a drift down but want to keep the shares: sell in the money and close or roll before expiry. For one-week calls he has no view; for one month he sells about 30 delta. You never have to lose your shares: close or roll, accepting a realized loss on the call against a gain on the stock.

steps.caption: A $100 stock with one-month covered calls.
Bullish view: sell about a 30 delta call at $105. You make the most at or above the strike.
Mildly bearish view: sell an in-the-money call at $95 for more protection.
The difference shows where each strike wins: up for OTM, flat or down for ITM.
Above the strike you may be assigned. Close or roll before expiry if you want to keep the shares.

takeaways: Strike choice follows your view of the stock at expiry.
Bullish: out of the money; drifting down: in the money.
You can always close or roll before expiry to keep the shares.
caveats: Stock legs conflict with the owner's options-only rule.
